newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech bank selloff plan seen in August - FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Czech bank selloff plan seen in August - FinMin.

text.p: Czech Finance Minister Ivan Pilip said on Tuesday that he would submit a general strategy for the privatisation of three of the country's four largest banks to the cabinet on August 20.

He told a news conference after a ministerial meeting that the government would seek an agreement with Slovakia -- which holds minority stakes in Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka (CSOB) and Komercni Banka a.s. -- over the future of the Slovak-held shares prior to privatisation.
"The privatisation of Komercni banka,. Ceska Sporitelna a.s. and CSOB should continue... and on August 20 material on the strategy will be submitted to the government," Pilip told reporters.
He said the ministers directed him and Czech National Bank Governor Josef Tosovsky to conduct talks with Slovak officials.
"It is one of the important problems which have to be solved before (the banks') privatisation is started," Pilip said.
He said that the talks should be part of a larger debate on outstanding claims by both countries connected to the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993.
Pilip added on Tuesday that the strategy should include options on the speed and forms of the banks' privatisation.
Various Slovak institutions hold a combined one-third stake in CSOB, while the investment fund VUB Kupon holds a 1.36 percent stake in Komercni.
Pilip submitted a previous plan to the cabinet in June, but it was sent back for further work. Ministers have not said what specifically was the problem with the original plan.
He added that the tender for the privatisation of a 36 percent stake in Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s. was in advanced stage but not finished.
"Our intention is to finish this privatisation in a short period," he said.
"I would like it to be a horizon shorter than month, but it depends on...finalising some partial questions which are left."
Nomura International and Dutch ING Bank NV are finalists in the government tender for IPB shares.

The ministry, directed by the cabinet in April to accelerate the pace of privatisation to help a lagging economy, said in early June that it planned to begin the further selloff this year of Komercni and CSOB shares.
It said the further privatisation of the largest retail savings bank, Ceska Sporitelna, was not planned for this year but possibly for 1998. The whole plan was returned by the government in June.
